title: Power Automate: view property values inline on cards in the new cloud flow designer
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout facts and maker-selected default match the roadmap, and its Layout route and product licensing are supported by Microsoft Learn. It reports the archived release plan's differing default and date without presenting that older plan as current guidance.

claims.claim: This feature belongs to Power Automate's new cloud flow designer.
claims.quote: Power Automate: Cloud flows - View property value expanded inline in new cloud flow designer

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Makers can view property values directly on action cards at design time.
claims.quote: When you add an action, you can view property values for multiple steps at design time, or output values for multiple steps at runtime. The inline view shows this information directly on the cards

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Data exposure; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The inline view can show output values on cards at runtime.
claims.quote: When you add an action, you can view property values for multiple steps at design time, or output values for multiple steps at runtime. The inline view shows this information directly on the cards

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Data exposure
claims.claim: Several steps' values can be viewed and compared at once.
claims.quote: The inline view shows this information directly on the cards, so you can review and compare values across several steps at once.

claims.claim: Without inline view, makers select each card individually to read its value in the side pane.
claims.quote: Without the inline view, you select each card individually to see its value in the side pane

claims.claim: The side pane value experience shows one step's value at a time.
claims.quote: you can view only one step's value at a time.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: According to the current roadmap, the side pane remains the default until a maker switches views.
claims.quote: You can choose which experience you prefer. The current side pane experience remains the default. You can switch to the inline view whenever you want and switch back at any time.

claims.where: What's changing; Change & support; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Makers can switch to the inline view and back at any time.
claims.quote: You can switch to the inline view whenever you want and switch back at any time.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists automatic availability for admins, makers and marketers rather than an administrator enablement requirement.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The current roadmap target is June CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The record supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap lists only Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope

claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap does not explicitly exclude GCC, GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The change is user-opt-in: makers choose the inline experience without a documented administrator switch.
claims.quote: You can choose which experience you prefer. The current side pane experience remains the default. You can switch to the inline view whenever you want and switch back at any time.

claims.claim: Included is the licensing model for this new view inside Power Automate's existing cloud automation capabilities.
claims.quote: With a Power Automate Premium user license, users gain the full set of capabilities for cloud and desktop automation

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Automate Premium includes the full set of cloud automation capabilities.
claims.quote: With a Power Automate Premium user license, users gain the full set of capabilities for cloud and desktop automation including premium connectors, process and task mining, AI Builder, use of managed environments, and Microsoft Dataverse storage.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licence specific to the inline view is published in the reviewed documentation or named in the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Automate" "inline" "layout" "license" "meter". Read Types of Power Automate licenses, Explore the cloud flows designer, the release-plan excerpt and the roadmap; none names a separate inline-view licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No meter specific to displaying inline values is published in the reviewed documentation or named in the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Automate" "inline" "layout" "license" "meter". Read Pay-as-you-go meters excerpts, Types of Power Automate licenses, the designer page and release-plan excerpt; meters describe flow runs, not displaying inline values.

claims.claim: The maker route is My flows > Cloud flows > flow > Edit > New designer (on) > Collapse (configuration pane) > Layout.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane to the left, select My flows. ... In the Cloud flows tab, select the flow you want to open. ... select Edit. ... Collapse button: (New designer only) Hide the pane. ... Layout: Switch between inline and panel layouts.

claims.claim: No API or automation operation is documented for the maker's designer layout selection.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate designer inline layout API PowerShell Power Platform API pac admin settings; "Power Automate Management" "designer" "layout". Read designer page, List tenant settings, pac admin and PowerShell support excerpts; no layout operation.

claims.claim: No tenant or environment UI setting or API is documented specifically for the inline property-value view as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate inline property value cloud flow designer admin disable tenant environment layout setting. Read designer and List tenant settings pages, plus Tenant settings, Manage Power Automate flows and pac admin excerpts; no inline-view switch.

claims.claim: Layout switches between inline and panel layouts.
claims.quote: Layout: Switch between inline and panel layouts.

claims.claim: The documented inline layout displays an action's properties in an expanded card on the canvas.
claims.quote: The inline layout displays an action's properties in an expanded card on the canvas.

claims.claim: The panel layout displays action properties in the configuration pane.
claims.quote: The panel layout displays the properties in the configuration pane on the left

claims.claim: The panel layout keeps action cards compact.
claims.quote: The panel layout displays the properties in the configuration pane on the left and keeps the action cards compact.

claims.claim: The designer documentation does not explicitly identify Layout as the switch for the roadmap's runtime property-value view.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Automate inline property value cloud flow designer admin disable tenant environment layout setting; "Power Automate Management" "designer" "layout". Read Explore the cloud flows designer and the release-plan excerpt; neither links Layout to runtime value display.

claims.claim: The designer overview documents inline action properties but does not describe displaying runtime output values on cards.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Automate Management" "designer" "layout". Read the full Explore the cloud flows designer page, including Canvas, Layout and Test; no runtime output-values-on-cards description.

claims.claim: The older release plan is archived, and its feature text remains available as a Learn search excerpt.
claims.quote: As of October 2026, this content is archived and no longer maintained.

claims.claim: The archived release-plan excerpt describes inline display as the default, unlike the current roadmap.
claims.quote: The feature shows all that information inline by default.

claims.claim: The archived release-plan excerpt gives February 2026 as the general-availability target.
claims.quote: | Enabled for | Public preview | Early access | General availability| ... | Admins, makers, marketers, or analysts, automatically | - | - | Feb 2026 |

claims.claim: The sources do not specify how inline runtime cards handle actions with Secure outputs enabled.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Automate" "inline" "Secure outputs". Read designer page, release-plan excerpt, Secure data used in cloud flows and Manage sensitive input like passwords excerpts; secure-output guidance covers logs, not inline runtime cards.

claims.claim: Secure outputs is an action setting available in the designer.
claims.quote: Use the Secure inputs and Secure outputs toggles to turn the operations, and references of output properties, on or off.

claims.claim: The roadmap description specifies no new permission.
claims.quote: You can choose which experience you prefer. The current side pane experience remains the default. You can switch to the inline view whenever you want and switch back at any time.

claims.claim: The roadmap description specifies no new connection.
claims.quote: The inline view shows this information directly on the cards, so you can review and compare values across several steps at once.

claims.claim: The roadmap description specifies no new identity.
claims.quote: You can be more efficient when authoring or debugging flows by using the inline view to examine property values from multiple steps at once without needing to select each step separately.

claims.claim: The roadmap names the new cloud flow designer without specifying another prerequisite.
claims.quote: Power Automate: Cloud flows - View property value expanded inline in new cloud flow designer

claims.claim: The documentation does not state whether this particular inline property and runtime-output view is offered in the classic designer.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Automate" "property value" "classic designer". Read designer overview, release-plan excerpt and classic-designer search excerpts; classic cards contain configuration data, but this particular runtime inline view is not identified there.

controlChecks.governs: Which layout a maker uses for action properties in the designer
